conflict: two active contracts assigned different meanings to a field both called 'pocket diameter'
resolution: NOT_A_VALUE_CONFLICT — A DATUM CONFLICT. The two numbers measure different things at different datums. Both are retained under explicit names and the ambiguous field name is retired.

entries.original_purpose: the PLAN-VIEW lattice module — the footprint reserved per pan so the 3x3 pitch can be resolved. It is a spacing reservation, never a cavity wall position at any elevation.
entries.derivation: 26.0 nominal pan + 2 x 0.30 manufacturing tolerance + 2 x 0.0 retention pocket add
entries.milestone_introduced: PALT-M1 / PALT-M2 (layout contract); the owner's M1 review explicitly corrected its class to CALCULATED_LAYOUT_HEURISTIC and NOT an industry or production standard
entries.note: pocket_module_mm(spec, PALT_P1_MECHANISM) returns exactly 26.6 only because ADHESIVE_FIXED retention adds 0.0. A retention strategy with a non-zero pocket add would move the module without moving any cavity wall — which is what proves the two quantities are independent.

entries.original_purpose: the moulded CAVITY diameter giving the metal pan radial seating clearance
entries.milestone_introduced: PALT-M4B (the module the owner declared INCOMPLETE)
entries.note: adopted as the A2 fit datum as an EXPLICIT DECISION, not inherited silently: it is the only one of the two that was ever defined as a cavity, and it is the value that lets a nominal pan seat. It still originates in an INCOMPLETE module, so it stays DESIGN_DEFAULT / NOT_MANUFACTURER_CONFIRMED.

entries.original_purpose: the visible mouth where the 0.6 mm rim fillet meets the flat deck
entries.derivation: sharp wall line at deck + 2 x rim fillet tangent offset
entries.note: a caliper on the top view reads this, not the fit datum. Reporting it as a discrepancy would be wrong — but the distinction has to be explicit and testable, which is what DATUMS provides.

retired_field.name: pocket_diameter_mm
retired_field.enforced_by: palette_recessed_tray_geometry.build_recessed_palette_tray raises RecessedTrayError when the key is present

unresolved: the 0.30 mm 'manufacturing tolerance' behind 26.6 is annotated 'pressed-powder pans have WIDE tolerance (R10)' — that is a POWDER/layout heuristic, not a drawn metal-pan shell tolerance. Using it as PAN_MAXIMUM_ENVELOPE is conservative and probably overstated. A real pan-shell tolerance is NOT_ESTABLISHED and needs a supplier drawing.
